An unlevered, cash-generating dairy with good three-year capital returns, in the middle of a procurement squeeze that has taken a fifth off operating profit and whose reported profit is being held up from below the operating line. points: Held — NESTLEIND is in your portfolio. Nestlé India, ₹2,37,723cr, Maggi, Nescafé, KitKat, Cerelac — the largest packaged-foods company in the country and by a wide margin the largest thing in this bucket, market_cap first of 32; promoters hold 62.76%. The tier is an artefact of a calendar change, not of size: Nestlé moved its year end from December to March, so the platform holds four annual rows and the oldest is a stub with sales present and the balance sheet wholly NULL. Maturity tier is derived from usable annual history, so a company incorporated in 1959 is bucketed mid-tier. No pillar percentile is quoted on this row for that reason, and the reading counts underneath them are thin enough to make it worse — 8 peers carry an operating margin here and 7 carry a TTM profit change.

What the bucket does to the ranks, concretely. The cohort is 32 names but the per-metric reading counts underneath it are far thinner: pe_ttm has 17 readings, opm_now 8, ttm_np_pct 7, div_yield 5, fii_pct 11. A position out of seven is not a rank, and a percentile built on a mixture of those counts is not a percentile. This row therefore quotes no pillar figure at all and argues from the company's own numbers, with peer ranks used only where the field is wide enough to carry one.

On its own figures the returns are extraordinary and the top line is not. roce_3y 105.92% is first of 29 — the highest return on capital in the bucket by a distance, which is what a brand portfolio with negative working capital produces; wc_days -73.82 is 32nd of 32, the most negative in the cohort. op_margin_3y 23.39% is second of 32 and np_consistency_3y 1.922 is first of 29. Against that rev_cagr_3y -2.57% is 27th of 29 and np_cagr_3y -5.68% is 21st of 27 — both three-year windows span the stub year, so they are measuring the calendar change as much as the business. That is the clearest single consequence of the year-end move.

The current year is genuinely strong, and the price reflects a decade of this. ttm_sales_pct +21.68%, ttm_op_pct +26.96% and ttm_np_pct +38.17% — profit growing faster than operating profit growing faster than sales, with opm_now 23.73% against opm_prev 22.74%. cfo_pat_3y 1.140 is eighth of 32, so it is cash. pb 46.10x is second of 31 and pe_ttm 60.39x; there is no own-history PE band because the usable annual history is four rows. debt_equity 0.086 is 27th of 31. tech_net_score_scaled is NULL for every scored company on the platform; the momentum pillar renormalises around the components that do exist, so the percentile is a narrower question than the scorecard asks rather than a lost weight.

Confidence is low because the scoring is, not because the business is. A 105.92% return on capital funded by negative working capital is as close to a structural moat as this platform measures, and it is being ranked against a bucket of mid-tier food companies because the year end moved. Hold on the business; do not read the pillar scores on this row, and do not compare the three-year growth figures to anything until a clean post-March history exists.

Three pillars of the four are built on missing components and the prose must say which. What can be measured is a very high margin and very fast growth. op_margin_3y 25.31% is first of 32 — the highest three-year operating margin in the mid-tier bucket. ttm_sales_pct +59.79%, ttm_op_pct +67.89% and ttm_np_pct +80.37% are each first in the field, and sales_yoy_q +39.53% is fourth of 13 — but those last four denominators are 8, 8, 7 and 13, so they are ranks against a handful of names and should be read as the company's own numbers rather than as positions.
